title: Quarterly trajectory grid and release-band scheduling for Hosted API & Model Catalog
creator: Asha Patel
project: Hosted API + Model Catalog Q2 Runway
description: Goal: Define a constraint-aware quarterly roadmap 'trajectory grid' that maps Hosted API release bands to Model Catalog commitments and OKR milestones. This ticket synthesizes capacity signals, canary windows, and cross-team dependencies into a release-band schedule (green/amber/red lanes) so product, infra, and GTM teams can plan commits and contingency hedges.
background: We receive frequent requests to make release commitments for hosted endpoints while preserving safety margins for capacity. Earlier approaches used single-point dates per model; that increased rollbacks and missed OKRs. The trajectory grid introduces release bands and week-level runway gates tied to capacity hedges and canary windows. This document is meant to be an operational artifact that feeds the quarterly planning deck and the cadence playbook.
decision_tradeoffs: Band-based scheduling (flexible window) reduces rollback risk but complicates external release communications.
Tighter fixed-date commitments improve external predictability at cost of higher failure/rollback probability when capacity or regressions appear.
Tie canary windows to model health signals rather than only calendar to reduce wasted capacity on safe rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Trajectory grid artifact (spreadsheet + visual) published to Confluence with band definitions and gating criteria
Mapping of each Hosted API model candidate to a release band and associated OKR milestone
Agreed contingency hedges and fallback models for each band
Dependencies and ownership annotated for infra, runtime, and eval teams
Stakeholder sign-off (PM, Infra ENG, Head of Console, Solutions) recorded

implementation_notes: Primary artifact: Confluence page 'Trajectory Grid Q2 2026' with CSV and visual heatmap
Data inputs: historical hosted API demand, Dedicated reserved capacity forecasts, model inference perf profiles
Runway lanes: green (low risk), amber (conditional), red (high risk / contingency only)
We will use runtime feature 'auto-fallback-to-variant' (ENG-1842) as primary mitigation for amber band incidents
Quantization/variant recommendations for each model to reduce peak token cost where possible
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Demand spike exhausts reserved capacity -> Mitigation: pre-signed burst capacity and priority routing
Risk: Model regression discovered in canary -> Mitigation: automatic rollback and traffic shift to previous variant
Risk: Cross-team misalignment on comms -> Mitigation: publish band-level stakeholder playbooks and weekly syncs
